criterion.summary: P_astro > 0.5 OR IFAR > 100 yr (either suffices); all 57 rows of Table 2 (label table:search) are the detections. Quotes are verbatim from the arXiv LaTeX source (math kept as LaTeX). Table numbers inferred from float order in the source.
criterion.quote: From the combined analysis of the 2015-2019 public LIGO and Virgo data, we find 55 BBH mergers and 2 BNS mergers. The list of gravitational wave mergers is given in Table~\ref{table:search}. For the majority of BBHs we can assess the probability of astrophysical origin. Our catalog includes candidates where $\mathcal{P}_{\textrm{astro}} > 0.5$ or $\mathrm{IFAR} > 100$ years. These thresholds are consistent with prior community conventions
criterion.section: Sec. 5 Observational Results (opening paragraph); same threshold in the Table 2 caption: "Gravitational-wave observations from the full search of O1-O3a data with $\mathcal{P}_{\textrm{astro}} > 0.5$ or IFAR $>$ 100 years."

tiers.name: detections (main table)
tiers.quote: Gravitational-wave observations from the full search of O1-O3a data with $\mathcal{P}_{\textrm{astro}} > 0.5$ or IFAR $>$ 100 years.

tiers.name: single-detector detections (more uncertain significance)
tiers.quote: We also show our estimates for single-detector candidates, which we note will necessarily be more uncertain, due to the need to extrapolate the background model. GW190425 is assessed using the same conservative extrapolation of the background as for BBH candidates
tiers.section: Table 2 caption; method in Sec. 3.3 Single-detector Candidates

tiers.name: near-threshold new detections
tiers.quote: We find four previously unreported BBH mergers; three, GW190725\_174728, GW190916\_200658, and GW190926\_050336 are near-threshold observations with relatively low SNR. The fourth, GW190925\_232845, has SNR $\sim 10$ and is found at a false alarm rate  $<1 / 100~ \textrm{years}$.

tiers.name: sub-threshold (NOT detections)
tiers.quote: In Table~\ref{table:sub} we show the 17 sub-threshold candidates with $\mathcal{P}_\mathrm{astro} > 0.2$ or IFAR $> 0.5$.

below_criterion.count_basis: Rows of Table 3 (label table:sub), stated as 17 in Sec. 5.3; parsed 17. None meets P_astro>0.5 or IFAR>100. The paper says the full sub-threshold set (O(10^6) candidates) is in the data release; only these 17 are tabulated.

named.note: Table 3; "was included in the 2-OGC catalog as a near threshold observation; in our updated analysis it is reduced in significance"
Table 3; "reported in 2-OGC as a sub-threshold event"
Not in any 3-OGC table; "Two marginal observations reported in Abbott:2020niy [GWTC-2], 190426_152155 and 190909_114149, are not assigned high significance in our analysis"
As above (GWTC-2 marginal, not assigned high significance by 3-OGC)

open_questions: GW190425_081805 is tabulated with P_astro = 0.50 and no IFAR, so strictly it does not satisfy "P_astro > 0.5" as printed (presumably rounding); the paper nevertheless counts it among the 57 and calls it robust.

Conclusions say "This includes 4 single-detector mergers in addition to 4 BBH mergers reported here for the first time", but Table 2 has 5 rows triggered in a single detector (GW190424_180648, GW190425_081805, GW190620_030421, GW190708_232457, GW190910_112807). Possibly the 4 means BBHs only (excluding BNS GW190425); not stated.
GW170817_124104 and GW190814_211039 have no P_astro (outside focused-BBH region) and qualify via IFAR > 100 yr only.
Several multi-detector detections qualify only via P_astro > 0.5 with IFAR well below 1 yr (e.g. GW190701_203306 IFAR 0.13 yr, GW190630_185205 IFAR 0.18 yr).
Table IFAR column is in years; FAR not tabulated separately (far left null).
